# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

Also let me now check the `_dart_duration_seconds` regex: `rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)"` — for name="seconds", the pattern `seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)`. Careful: "milliseconds" contains "seconds" as a substring! The loop iterates over factors dict: milliseconds first, then seconds. For a declaration `Duration(seconds: 30)`, the "milliseconds" pattern `milliseconds\s*:\s*...` doesn't match. For `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`, "milliseconds" matches and adds 0.5. Then the "seconds" pattern: `seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)` — does "milliseconds: 500" contain a match for `seconds\s*:`? "milliseconds: 500" — the substring "seconds: 500" IS present within "milliseconds: 500"! The regex `seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)` would match at position of "seconds" inside "milliseconds", extracting 500 → adding 500*1.0 = 500 seconds! That's a parsing bug: `Duration(milliseconds: 500)` would parse as 0.5 + 500 = 500.5 seconds.

Wait let me double check: `re.findall(rf"seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", "milliseconds: 500")` — the string "milliseconds: 500" contains "seconds: 500" starting at index 7 ("milli" + "seconds"). findall scans for non-overlapping matches: yes, it finds "seconds: 500" and captures "500". So `total += 500.0 * 1.0`.

And "milliseconds" was matched first: `milliseconds\s*:\s*([0.9]+)` finds "500" → total += 0.5.

So `Duration(milliseconds: 500)` parses as 500.5 seconds instead of 0.5s. **BUG** in the helper — but does it matter for the REG's actual use? The REG parses `providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5)` — only "minutes" matches. But the docstring explicitly advertises: "Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`, `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`, `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the parse must survive a benign unit change there." That's a false failure — the helper is buggy for the exact cases its own docstring claims to support. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

So the gh-1430 test group in `agent_cli_thinking_stream_test.dart` does NOT include a stream-json/HEP E5 test (no streamJson/hep references in that file). The ticket's edge case E5 says: "stream-json/HEP modes: heartbeat must not corrupt the FIRST-line contract (headers write before any event; heartbeat only during a request)" and the test plan IT-H1..H3 mentions "heartbeat line never interleaves into a JSON/HEP first line — header race pin".

Is the heartbeat even ARMED in stream-json mode? The gate is `_useTui || config.streamThinking`. In stream-json headless mode, `_useTui` is false and streamThinking defaults false → the heartbeat IS armed and CAN print. The print goes through `_printLiveness` → `io.writeln` → stderr in headless (per the CliIO contract "route [CliIO.writeln] diagnostics to stderr"). So stdout stays clean IF the host io is wired to stderr. Is that guaranteed for stream-json mode? The doc comment says "should be non-interactive and route CliIO.writeln diagnostics to stderr" — it's a contract on the host wiring, not enforced. The pre-existing tier-2 line has the same exposure, and the HEP/stream-json tests pass today (gh-1198 shipped with the same channel). So E5 risk is inherited, not new. The missing E5 IT is a test-coverage gap vs the ticket's stated test plan (IT-H1..H3 "header race pin"). Since behavior is safe by the same channel as tier-2, I'd rate the missing E5 test as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-borderline. Given the ticket explicitly promised "IT-H1..H3: abort-mid-heartbeat cleanliness (heartbeat line never interleaves into a JSON/HEP first line — header race pin)" and no such test exists, that's a legitimate coverage gap worth flagging — IMPORTANT? Hmm. The PR description's test list doesn't claim an E5 test: "headless ITs — stdout growth under a thinking-only stream (AC3), event-silent silence, tier-2-only dead window, non-reasoning byte-identity (AC5), `--stream-thinking` unchanged, tool-row disarm/re-arm (E2), line-mode parity, compaction window (E3)". So the PR itself doesn't claim E5 coverage — the ticket's test plan listed it, though. E4 (abort/Ctrl-C mid-heartbeat: pending timer cancels; no line after the abort banner) — is there a test? I don't see an explicit E4 abort test in the new tests either. The lifecycle `stop()` UT covers disarm-on-stop; the `_printLiveness` `_cli._exited` guard covers the print-after-exit. But "abort mid-heartbeat → no line after the abort banner" is not directly tested. Again a promised-in-ticket test that's missing.

Now, AC1 in the ticket: "the moment a renderable byte prints (text delta / tool line / streamed thinking), the heartbeat disarms. UT with fake clock + fake event sink." ✓ covered by UTs.

AC3: "headless E2E: a fake provider streaming thinking-only deltas for 6 minutes leaves the captured stdout byte-count monotonically growing (heartbeat cadence visible); no provider error; run completes." The IT test uses `streamLivenessTickForTest()` manual ticks rather than real timer-driven 6-minute flow — acceptable harness-level equivalent (fake clock + manual tick seam). The ticket says "fake clock + fake event sink" for AC1 UT; AC3 E2E with real timers would need 6 minutes — the IT uses the tick seam. Reasonable adaptation.

AC4: ✓ REG-R3 shipped + in-code invariant in the module docstring. ✓ verified the Dart line parses (300s).

And the parse: the line `const providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);` — `stripped.startswith("const providerStreamIdleTimeout =")` ✓. `_dart_duration_seconds("const providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);")`:
- index("(") → first "(" — that's in `Duration(`. Wait — "const providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);" — the first "(" is at "Duration(". ✓. rindex(")") → the ")" after 5. body = "minutes: 5". ✓ → 300.0.

But the milliseconds-bug: `re.findall(rf"seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body)` — I should verify the substring problem concretely. "milliseconds: 500" — regex "seconds\s*:" finds "seconds: 500"? The string contains "milli**seconds**: 500". The regex matches "seconds: 500" (findall returns all non-overlapping matches, capturing 500). So yes → 500 added. Today it's fed only `Duration(minutes: 5)` so the REG passes, but the claimed unit-change resilience is broken for the milliseconds case. IMPORTANT (test-helper correctness), maybe SUGGESTION? So there's no explicit shutdown `stop()` for either tracker in `agent_cli.dart`; `_printLiveness` guards against printing after exit (`_cli._exited`), and the timer chain self-cancels on next tick when disarmed. This matches the pre-existing tier-2 design (same risk profile), so not a new issue introduced by this PR. The heartbeat follows the exact same pattern as the sibling tracker. OK.

Now — a significant design check: **the `streamHeartbeat`'s production timer leg vs the "event-driven, never a wall timer" invariant.** The heartbeat uses the same one-shot Timer chain as tier 2: `requestStarted()` → `_arm()` schedules a tick at `toolLivenessTickSeconds`. The tick fires and `_evaluate()` prints ONLY if dirty. So the timer legs are wall timers but the PRINT is event-gated. Good — a dead stream never prints. ✓.

But there's a subtle interplay: `_evaluate` computes `elapsed = _clock().difference(since).inSeconds` and prints `… reasoning {elapsed}s (streaming)`. The elapsed is from REQUEST START, not from the first event. In the test `test_single_stall_gap...` no wait, that's Python. In the IT: request starts, thinking deltas arrive ~instantly, tick at t=60 → "… reasoning 60s (streaming)". OK — elapsed counts from request start. Documented in the UT ("elapsed counts from the request start"). Fine.

**Another check — the tier-2 + heartbeat double-print in the AC2 IT**: request with NO events → tier-2 prints bare lines; heartbeat armed but not dirty → silent. ✓ (tested).

**What about the case where events flow and THEN rendered output happens but the message continues?** e.g., thinking deltas → heartbeat prints at 60s → text delta arrives → disarm. ✓.

**What about `TurnEndEvent` → stop() but the turn continues with tool calls?** Tool calls → ToolExecutionStartEvent → renderedOutput → stop (no-op). After the tool ends, the next request re-arms. ✓.

**Edge: `MessageStartEvent` for the USER prompt.** In `_onAgentEvent`, every event that is not ModelRequestEvent goes through `reasoningProgress(event)`. The user prompt message start happens BEFORE ModelRequestEvent? Let me check the agent loop emission order: prompt → AgentStartEvent, TurnStartEvent, MessageStart(user message)... then ModelRequestEvent (before StreamFunction runs). If MessageStart(user) precedes ModelRequestEvent, then `streamHeartbeatProgress` sees MessageStartEvent → `unrenderedEvent()` → tracker not armed → no-op ✓. And `reasoning.progress()` → not armed → no-op ✓.

But wait — order could also be: MessageStartEvent(user prompt) → MessageEndEvent(user prompt). `MessageEndEvent` → `streamHeartbeat.stop()` — no-op while disarmed ✓.

Now the potentially problematic one: **`MessageEndEvent` for a TOOL RESULT message**. Sequence after a tool executes: ToolExecutionEndEvent → renderedOutput (stop). Tool result message added: MessageStartEvent(toolResult) → unrenderedEvent (no-op, disarmed). MessageEndEvent(toolResult) → stop (no-op). Then ModelRequestEvent → re-arm ✓.

Hmm, but what if the ORDER is: MessageStart(toolResult) fires while the tracker is still armed? Possible if a turn ends with tool calls and no MessageEnd for the assistant? No — the assistant message ends (MessageEndEvent assistant → stop) before tools execute. So by tool time, tracker is disarmed. ✓.

**Another edge — `MessageUpdateEvent` non-delta events**: ToolCallStartEvent/ToolCallEndEvent arrive as MessageUpdateEvent (they're AssistantMessageEvents). Headless does NOT render tool-call message events (the tool ROW comes from ToolExecutionStartEvent — agent-level). Wait, does headless print anything on ToolCallStartEvent? Looking at `_onMessageUpdate` — it handles TextDeltaEvent and ThinkingDeltaEvent only. So ToolCallStart/End as message events → unrenderedEvent → marks dirty. But immediately after, ToolExecutionStartEvent (agent event) → renderedOutput → stop. In between there's no tick. So the dirty mark is harmless. ✓.

Hmm wait, actually there's one interesting case: what does `DoneEvent` map to? DoneEvent is an AssistantMessageEvent → MessageUpdateEvent → not Text/Thinking → unrenderedEvent → dirty. Then MessageEndEvent fires → stop. Fine.

**Now the biggest design question: does the heartbeat actually keep the pane growing during a LONG thinking burst in real bench conditions?** The production timer leg: `requestStarted` arms a timer at `toolLivenessTickSeconds` (default? let me check `defaultToolLivenessTickSeconds`). If the default tick is e.g. 1s and liveness cadence 30s, then during thinking: dirty at first event, tick at 1s (elapsed < 30 → silent, dirty preserved ✓), ... at 30s → print, dirty=false. Then continued deltas re-dirty. Each subsequent tick (1s later) → elapsed 31 >= 30 and dirty (if deltas flowed since the print) → print again! **This means after the first print, the heartbeat prints EVERY TICK (every 1s) as long as thinking deltas keep flowing.** Hmm wait — re-read `_evaluate`:

```dart
if (elapsed < threshold) return;  // not printed, dirty preserved
_dirty = false;
_onRemind(elapsed);
```

After a print at t=30, the next tick at t=31: dirty=true (deltas flowed), elapsed=31 >= 30 → prints again. So from t=30 onward, it prints EVERY tickSeconds (1s) as long as events keep flowing. That's a line-per-second after the first 30s! Compare tier 2, which has the same structure (fire when elapsed >= remindAfter, then... wait — tier 2 doesn't clear anything; it re-fires EVERY tick once past the threshold: `_evaluate` in tier-2 has no state clear, so tier-2 prints every tick past the threshold too!).

Hold on — tier-2 `tick()`: cancel timer, `_evaluate()`, re-arm. `_evaluate`: if elapsed >= remindAfter → `_onRemind(elapsed)`. There's no "reset the elapsed base" — the comment says "re-arm a full cadence from NOW" but the elapsed base (`_since`) is NOT reset; only the timer leg is. So tier 2 prints every TICK (not every cadence) once elapsed >= cadence. With tickSeconds default = ? Let me check `defaultToolLivenessTickSeconds` and what the CLI configures.

If tick is 1s and cadence 30s: tier-2 prints at 30, 31, 32, ... one line per second. Hmm, that seems spammy — but that's PRE-EXISTING gh-1198 behavior, not this PR. Let me verify the defaults.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

The headless doc says: "The host's [CliIO] should be non-interactive and route [CliIO.writeln] diagnostics to stderr so [CliIO.write] (the assistant text) is the only stdout content."

So in headless mode, `io.writeln` (used by `_printLiveness`) goes to **stderr**, not stdout. That's how the tier-2 line stays off the structured stdout channel. The heartbeat uses the same `_printLiveness` → same channel. So E5 is safe by construction, same as tier 2 (gh-1198). The ticket says "the heartbeat only prints where tier 2 already printed ... through the same `_printLiveness` stderr channel". ✓.

But wait — is that true in LINE MODE (interactive)? In line mode, `io.writeln` goes to stdout, interleaving prose — that's the intended surface ("the prose channel"). Fine.

So the gh-1430 test group in `agent_cli_thinking_stream_test.dart` does NOT include a stream-json/HEP E5 test (no streamJson/hep references in that file). The ticket's edge case E5 says: "stream-json/HEP modes: heartbeat must not corrupt the FIRST-line contract (headers write before any event; heartbeat only during a request)" and the test plan IT-H1..H3 mentions "heartbeat line never interleaves into a JSON/HEP first line — header race pin".

Is the heartbeat even ARMED in stream-json mode? The gate is `_useTui || config.streamThinking`. In stream-json headless mode, `_useTui` is false and streamThinking defaults false → the heartbeat IS armed and CAN print. The print goes through `_printLiveness` → `io.writeln` → stderr in headless (per the CliIO contract "route [CliIO.writeln] diagnostics to stderr"). So stdout stays clean IF the host io is wired to stderr. Is that guaranteed for stream-json mode? The doc comment says "should be non-interactive and route CliIO.writeln diagnostics to stderr" — it's a contract on the host wiring, not enforced. The pre-existing tier-2 line has the same exposure, and the HEP/stream-json tests pass today (gh-1198 shipped with the same channel). So E5 risk is inherited, not new. The missing E5 IT is a test-coverage gap vs the ticket's stated test plan (IT-H1..H3 "header race pin"). Since behavior is safe by the same channel as tier-2, I'd rate the missing E5 test as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-borderline. Given the ticket explicitly promised "IT-H1..H3: abort-mid-heartbeat cleanliness (heartbeat line never interleaves into a JSON/HEP first line — header race pin)" and no such test exists, that's a legitimate coverage gap worth flagging — IMPORTANT? Hmm. The PR description's test list doesn't claim an E5 test: "headless ITs — stdout growth under a thinking-only stream (AC3), event-silent silence, tier-2-only dead window, non-reasoning byte-identity (AC5), `--stream-thinking` unchanged, tool-row disarm/re-arm (E2), line-mode parity, compaction window (E3)". So the PR itself doesn't claim E5 coverage — the ticket's test plan listed it, though. E4 (abort/Ctrl-C mid-heartbeat: pending timer cancels; no line after the abort banner) — is there a test? I don't see an explicit E4 abort test in the new tests either. The lifecycle `stop()` UT covers disarm-on-stop; the `_printLiveness` `_cli._exited` guard covers the print-after-exit. But "abort mid-heartbeat → no line after the abort banner" is not directly tested. Again a promised-in-ticket test that's missing.

Now, AC1 in the ticket: "the moment a renderable byte prints (text delta / tool line / streamed thinking), the heartbeat disarms. UT with fake clock + fake event sink." ✓ covered by UTs.

AC3: "headless E2E: a fake provider streaming thinking-only deltas for 6 minutes leaves the captured stdout byte-count monotonically growing (heartbeat cadence visible); no provider error; run completes." The IT test uses `streamLivenessTickForTest()` manual ticks rather than real timer-driven 6-minute flow — acceptable harness-level equivalent (fake clock + manual tick seam). The ticket says "fake clock + fake event sink" for AC1 UT; AC3 E2E with real timers would need 6 minutes — the IT uses the tick seam. Reasonable adaptation.

AC4: ✓ REG-R3 shipped + in-code invariant in the module docstring. ✓ verified the Dart line parses (300s).

Wait — one thing to double-check on the REG: it reads `lib/src/providers/provider_common.dart` from `root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[2]`. test file is `bench/terminal_bench/test_fa_agent_timeout.py` → parents[0]=terminal_bench, parents[1]=bench, parents[2]=repo root. ✓.

And the parse: the line `const providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);` — `stripped.startswith("const providerStreamIdleTimeout =")` ✓. But wait — is there any OTHER line in that file starting with `const providerStreamIdleTimeout =`? Line 828 only (925 is `providerTimeoutsOverride?...`). The loop takes the FIRST match. ✓.

`_dart_duration_seconds("const providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);")`:
- index("(") → first "(" — that's in `Duration(`. Wait — "const providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5);" — the first "(" is at "Duration(". ✓. rindex(")") → the ")" after 5. body = "minutes: 5". ✓ → 300.0.
- margin 60 → requires >= 360. `_STALL_GAP_DEFAULT` = 360.0 ✓ (boundary-inclusive assertGreaterEqual).

But the milliseconds-bug: `re.findall(rf"seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body)` — I should verify the substring problem concretely. "milliseconds: 500" — regex "seconds\s*:" finds "seconds: 500"? The string contains "milli**seconds**: 500". The regex matches "seconds: 500" (findall returns all non-overlapping matches, capturing 500). So yes → 500 added. Confirmed bug in the helper for `Duration(milliseconds: ...)`, contradicting its own docstring. Today it's fed only `Duration(minutes: 5)` so the REG passes, but the claimed unit-change resilience is broken for the milliseconds case. IMPORTANT (test-helper correctness), maybe SUGGESTION? The helper's docstring explicitly promises `Duration(milliseconds: 500)` works. A benign unit change to milliseconds would make the REG compute a watchdog 1000x too large → false failure... wait: `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)` (5 min in ms) → "milliseconds" matches → 300; "seconds" substring also matches → 3000 seconds → watchdog_sec = 300 → assertion 360 >= 300360 fails → REG fails spuriously. A false BLOCKING failure on a benign refactor. That's a real defect in shipped test code — I'd rate IMPORTANT (the PR works as shipped; the helper is wrong for the exact cases it advertises).

Let me quickly verify this with python to be sure.

Then other checks:
- `bench/fa_agent_timeout.py` full read for context around changed lines.
- `bench/post_mortem_usage.py` — behavior change: `post_mortem(runs_dir)` called with no gap now uses 360 instead of 240. Tests updated? test_post_mortem_usage passed ✓.
- Check `bench/terminal_bench/summary.py` line 377 — `max_gap < bench_metrics.DEFAULT_STALL_GAP_SEC` now 360 — consistent.
- Backward-compat: `FA_STALL_GAP_SEC` env still overrides; `post_mortem(stall_gap_sec=...)` callers passing 240 explicitly? `main()` calls `post_mortem(argv[1])` — default now 360 ✓.

Now the Dart-side remaining concerns:

A. **`reasoningProgress(event)` is called for EVERY agent event, including `ToolCallHeartbeatEvent`s etc. — `reasoning.progress()` disarms tier 2 on ANY event (pre-existing behavior). ✓ unchanged.

B. **`streamHeartbeatProgress` `default: break;`** — events like `AgentStartEvent`, `TurnStartEvent`, `ModelRequestEvent`(handled separately), `ToolPairingRepairEvent`, `TaskLedgerEvent`, `ToolExecutionUpdateEvent`, `ToolCallHeartbeatEvent`, `ToolCallStuckEvent`, `AgentSettledEvent` — left untouched. Hmm: `AgentSettledEvent` — fires after AgentEndEvent; stop already happened. `ToolExecutionUpdateEvent` (partial tool results) — rendered? In headless, does `_onToolExecutionUpdate` print? Tool heartbeats print `⏳` lines? The `⏳` tool liveness lines print via `_printLiveness` on the liveness tracker cadence — those are rendered BYTES on the pane! A `⏳ [bash] sleep 500 — running 120s` line prints bytes. But `ToolCallHeartbeatEvent` (gh-1054 session-record heartbeat, "the terminal stays quiet") doesn't print. The gh-1055 tracker lines are timer-driven, not event-driven. OK — leaving those untouched is right (they're not stream events; they'd wrongly "prove stream aliveness"... actually wait, would they? If a tool runs long and the gh-1055 ⏳ line prints, the pane grows — good for the bench — and the stream heartbeat stays armed from the request... hmm, no: ToolExecutionStartEvent → renderedOutput → stop. So during tool execution the stream heartbeat is OFF; the ⏳ liveness lines own that window. ✓ architecture is coherent.

C. **Potential missed window**: between `TurnEndEvent` (stop) and the next `ModelRequestEvent` (arm) — the turn-boundary bookkeeping (persist, follow-ups) — pane-silent but short. Fine.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

But there's a subtle interplay: `_evaluate` computes `elapsed = _clock().difference(since).inSeconds` and prints `… reasoning {elapsed}s (streaming)`. The elapsed is from REQUEST START, not from the first event. In the test `test_single_stall_gap...` no wait, that's Python. # AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

```dart
providerTimeoutsOverride?.streamIdle ?? providerStreamIdleTimeout;
```

So the effective watchdog can be LOWERED via `providerTimeoutsOverride.streamIdle` (config). Also `providerStreamIdleTimeoutForUrl` — there's a per-URL override function! The ordering invariant (gap >= watchdog) holds even more comfortably when the watchdog is shorter. The risk is the watchdog getting LONGER — which the REG catches for the const. Also let me now check the `_dart_duration_seconds` regex: `rf"{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)"` — for name="seconds", the pattern `seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)`. Careful: "milliseconds" contains "seconds" as a substring! The loop iterates over factors dict: milliseconds first, then seconds. For a declaration `Duration(seconds: 30)`, the "milliseconds" pattern `milliseconds\s*:\s*...` doesn't match. For `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`, "milliseconds" matches and adds 0.5. Then the "seconds" pattern: `seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)` — does "milliseconds: 500" contain a match for `seconds\s*:`? "milliseconds: 500" — the substring "seconds: 500" IS present within "milliseconds: 500"! The regex `seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)` would match at position of "seconds" inside "milliseconds", extracting 500 → adding 500*1.0 = 500 seconds! That's a parsing bug: `Duration(milliseconds: 500)` would parse as 0.5 + 500 = 500.5 seconds.

Wait let me double check: `re.findall(rf"seconds\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", "milliseconds: 500")` — the string "milliseconds: 500" contains "seconds: 500" starting at index 7 ("milli" + "seconds"). findall scans for non-overlapping matches: yes, it finds "seconds: 500" and captures "500". So `total += 500.0 * 1.0`.

And "milliseconds" was matched first: `milliseconds\s*:\s*([0.9]+)` finds "500" → total += 0.5.

So `Duration(milliseconds: 500)` parses as 500.5 seconds instead of 0.5s. **BUG** in the helper — but does it matter for the REG's actual use? The REG parses `providerStreamIdleTimeout = Duration(minutes: 5)` — only "minutes" matches. But the docstring explicitly advertises: "Accepts any argument subset/order (`Duration(seconds: 180)`, `Duration(minutes: 5)`, `Duration(minutes: 1, seconds: 30)`, `Duration(milliseconds: 500)`) — the parse must survive a benign unit change there." So if someone changes the Dart to `Duration(milliseconds: 3000)`, the REG would compute 3000*0.001 + 3000*1.0 = 300 — hmm wait: for "milliseconds: 3000": "milliseconds" factor matches → 300; "seconds" pattern also matches inside → 3000 seconds. That's a false failure — the helper is buggy for the exact cases its own docstring claims to support. Since the helper is only fed one specific line today, it's not a live bug, but it contradicts the stated contract. Severity: IMPORTANT (test helper correctness; would produce a confusing false failure on a benign unit change — exactly the scenario the helper was written to survive).

Actually `\b` between "i" and "s" — both word chars → no boundary → `\bseconds` would NOT match inside "milliseconds". Let me verify: regex `\bseconds` against "milliseconds": position before "seconds" in "milliseconds" is between 'i' and 's', both word characters, so no word boundary → no match. So `rf"\b{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)"` fixes it. Or match `(?:^|[{,\s]){name}`.

So there's no explicit shutdown `stop()` for either tracker in `agent_cli.dart`; `_printLiveness` guards against printing after exit (`_cli._exited`), and the timer chain self-cancels on next tick when disarmed. This matches the pre-existing tier-2 design (same risk profile), so not a new issue introduced by this PR. The heartbeat follows the exact same pattern as the sibling tracker. OK.

Now — a significant design check: **the `streamHeartbeat`'s production timer leg vs the "event-driven, never a wall timer" invariant.** The heartbeat uses the same one-shot Timer chain as tier 2: `requestStarted()` → `_arm()` schedules a tick at `toolLivenessTickSeconds`. The tick fires and `_evaluate()` prints ONLY if dirty. So the timer legs are wall timers but the PRINT is event-gated. Good — a dead stream never prints. ✓.

But there's a subtle interplay: `_evaluate` computes `elapsed = _clock().difference(since).inSeconds` and prints `… reasoning {elapsed}s (streaming)`. The elapsed is from REQUEST START, not from the first event. In the test `test_single_stall_gap...` no wait, that's Python. In the IT: request starts, thinking deltas arrive ~instantly, tick at t=60 → "… reasoning 60s (streaming)". OK — elapsed counts from request start. Documented in the UT ("elapsed counts from the request start"). Fine.

**Another check — the tier-2 + heartbeat double-print in the AC2 IT**: request with NO events → tier-2 prints bare lines; heartbeat armed but not dirty → silent. ✓ (tested).

**What about the case where events flow and THEN rendered output happens but the message continues?** e.g., thinking deltas → heartbeat prints at 60s → text delta arrives → disarm. ✓.

**What about `TurnEndEvent` → stop() but the turn continues with tool calls?** Tool calls → ToolExecutionStartEvent → renderedOutput → stop (no-op). After the tool ends, the next request re-arms. ✓.

**Edge: `MessageStartEvent` for the USER prompt.** In `_onAgentEvent`, every event that is not ModelRequestEvent goes through `reasoningProgress(event)`. The user prompt message start happens BEFORE ModelRequestEvent? Let me check the agent loop emission order: prompt → AgentStartEvent, TurnStartEvent, MessageStart(user message)... then ModelRequestEvent (before StreamFunction runs). If MessageStart(user) precedes ModelRequestEvent, then `streamHeartbeatProgress` sees MessageStartEvent → `unrenderedEvent()` → tracker not armed → no-op ✓. And `reasoning.progress()` → not armed → no-op ✓.

But wait — order could also be: MessageStartEvent(user prompt) → MessageEndEvent(user prompt). `MessageEndEvent` → `streamHeartbeat.stop()` — no-op while disarmed ✓.

# AGENTS.md

Conventions for AI agents and contributors in this repository. Keep it
factual: paths, commands, invariants — no essays.

## Project layout

- `lib/` — the `flutter_agent_harness` package (pure Dart core). `test/`
  mirrors it. `prompts/` — all LLM prompts as Markdown (see rules below).
- `lib/flutter_agent_harness.dart` (the barrel) — gh-1232 policy:
  GROUPED APPEND-ONLY export sections, one `// ── <subsystem> ──` comment
  header per group, exports sorted by path within a group, new exports
  appended to their subsystem group (a new subsystem starts a new group).
  No per-subsystem mini-barrels, no re-sorting of existing lines — append
  only, so parallel edits almost never touch the same line.
- God-file ceiling (gh-1232): no Dart file over 2800 lines anywhere
  (crap4dart `loc` gate, `max_lines: 2800` — issue #1234 migrated the
  shell guards; enforced whole-tree in CI and on staged files by the
  pre-commit hook. Scope: core `lib bin` via `crap4dart.yaml` +
  `test example` via the `crap4dart.loc-scope.yaml` companion config
  (0.11.0 has no per-gate sources override), flutter_app/lib via
  `flutter_app/crap4dart.yaml`).
  Target < 2000 for primary
  files; when a file approaches it, split by concern into `part` files
  (the established pattern: `agent_cli.dart`, `builtin_tools.dart`,
  `bin/fah.dart` → `bin/fah_*.dart`, `agent_service.dart` →
  `agent_service_*.dart` mixins) — never by extracting public API.
- `lib/src/approval/` — tool approval gate: tiers (read/write/exec),
  session modes (always-ask/write/yolo/autopilot — the CLI label of the
  `unattended` enum), per-tool overrides,
  critical-pattern
  `bash` interceptor, per-turn grants (`grantForTurn(allow:, deny:)` —
  skill `allowed-tools`/`disallowed-tools` manifest keys ride these for one
  turn; explicit deny > turnDeny > per-tool override > turnAllow >
  alwaysAllow > mode (critical bash outranks mode in always-ask/write/yolo,
  but is skipped in unattended so the mode never blocks — for runs with no
  user present); `clearTurnGrants()`
  on every new user
  message). Wired via `attachApproval` into `beforeToolCall` (runs
  first); prompt UI is an injectable `ApprovalPrompt` (null + prompt policy
  = deny).
- `lib/src/tools/ask_tool.dart` — `ask` tool: structured mid-turn questions
  via injectable `AskCallback` (null = error, cancel = plain result).
- `lib/src/tools/request_secret_tool.dart` — `request_secret` tool: the agent
  asks the USER for a missing credential via injectable
  `RequestSecretCallback` (never in chat text); a grant returns
  `RequestSecretResult` (host-adjusted `name`, `value`, `persisted` flag),
  a decline is a plain result. The app wires it in `AgentService` to
  `secretRequestHandler` (chat screen installs
  `ui/widgets/secret_request_sheet.dart`): a grant is persisted into
  `SessionKeysStore`, injected into the live shell env via
  `SecretsExecutionEnv.addSecrets` (the map is runtime-mutable now), and
  registered into the same `SecretRedactor` — so the next run's prompt name
  list, bash `$NAME`, and redaction all pick it up.
- `lib/src/env/session_vars_execution_env.dart` — `SessionVarsExecutionEnv`:
  an `ExecutionEnv` decorator injecting session-correlation env vars
  (`FAH_SESSION_ID`/`FAH_SESSION_FILE`/`FAH_PROVIDER`/`FAH_MODEL`, resolved
  live per `exec`, never secrets) into bash tool executions. Wired around
  `builtinTools` in the CLI (`AgentCli`) and the app (`AgentService`).
  `LocalShell` merges `ShellExecOptions.env` OVER `Platform.environment`
  (never replaces), so injected vars keep the inherited environment.
- `lib/src/env/io_execution_env.dart` — `LocalShell`: foreground `exec`
  runs under `setsid` when the host has it (probe
  `ownProcessGroupAvailable`, seam `ownProcessGroupOverride`) and the
  timeout/cancel paths reap the whole tree (`killTree` + direct-kill
  backstop) with a capped pipe-drain (`_drainGrace`) — timeout/cancel'd
  calls complete in ≤ timeout + kill grace + drain grace; a no-timeout
  call within `_drainGrace` of the direct child's exit (the drain is
  capped unconditionally: after the child is reaped every remaining pipe
  byte comes from an orphan). Killed calls are marked `timeout`/`aborted`
  and carry the captured partial output on `ExecutionError.stdout`/
  `stderr` — tail-capped at the source to the last 64 KiB (`_captureTail`)
  — rendered by the bash tool and the skill renderer's `!cmd` failure
  branch (every string that branch embeds is tail-capped to ~2 KB)
  (gh-1053; the timeout timer stays
  armed after the child exits because an orphaned descendant can hold
  the pipes — a drain that outlives the deadline marks the call
  `timedOut` even when the child exited 0). Background jobs (issue #517)
  keep their own group + `stop()` semantics.
- `lib/src/tools/checkpoint_tool.dart` — `checkpoint`/`rewind` tools:
