# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) …

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

Interesting — the `liveness_bytes_of` helper only counts lines with the `⏳` anchor (gh-1055 tool-liveness family). The docstring added in this PR says:

"Extension signal (E1): the counters fed to ProgressLadder measure the agent process's own output bytes. The harness itself emits nothing into that stream on a timer — EXCEPT fa's own liveness lines (the ⏳ tool liveness family and, since gh-1430, the `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` heartbeat), which are fa's designed in-band liveness signal and are documented, not subtracted (see audit_dict / liveness_bytes_of)."

But `liveness_bytes_of` only detects `⏳` lines — the new `… reasoning Ns (streaming)` heartbeat lines are NOT counted by it. So `progress_liveness_bytes` in the audit will UNDERCOUNT: heartbeat bytes count as progress in the pane counter but are invisible to the liveness-bytes disclosure. The docstring says "documented, not subtracted (see audit_dict / liveness_bytes_of)" — the audit does NOT document heartbeat bytes; it only documents ⏳ bytes. This makes the AC8-style audit slightly dishonest: a trial kept alive purely by reasoning heartbeats would show `progress_liveness_bytes: 0`-ish while the pane growth was entirely heartbeat-originated.

Is that a real problem? The audit's purpose (issue #1185 AC6) is to make liveness-inflation VISIBLE per trial. The PR extends the family of fa-originated liveness lines but doesn't extend the detector. The fix is trivial: `_LIVENESS_ANCHOR`-family check to also count "… reasoning" lines (or `"(streaming)"`). The PR's own comment points readers to liveness_bytes_of as the place this is "documented" — but it isn't there. I'd rate this IMPORTANT (audit honesty gap; misleading pointer), arguably not blocking since the bench kill decision itself is what matters and the gap only affects per-trial audit disclosure.

Hmm, wait — actually, let me reconsider. `liveness_bytes_of` measures bytes in the PROGRESS SAMPLE fed to the ladder (the fa_agent.py adapter reads the progress log and computes liveness bytes). Where is `liveness_bytes_of` called from? Let me check fa_agent.py / wherever. If the audit inflates progress with heartbeat bytes without disclosing, the round-2-style "score honesty" analysis could misread. It's a disclosure gap. IMPORTANT.

Also note the docstring in fa_agent.py: "fa's own liveness lines ... are fa's designed in-band liveness signal and are documented, not subtracted (issue #1122 E1, gh-1430)". Same claim.

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

```python
for value in re.findall(rf"\b{name}\s*:\s*([0-9.]+)", body):
```

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) …

So the gh-1430 test group in `agent_cli_thinking_stream_test.dart` does NOT include a stream-json/HEP E5 test (no streamJson/hep references in that file). The ticket's edge case E5 says: "stream-json/HEP modes: heartbeat must not corrupt the FIRST-line contract (headers write before any event; heartbeat only during a request)" and the test plan IT-H1..H3 mentions "heartbeat line never interleaves into a JSON/HEP first line — header race pin".

Is the heartbeat even ARMED in stream-json mode? The gate is `_useTui || config.streamThinking`. In stream-json headless mode, `_useTui` is false and streamThinking defaults false → the heartbeat IS armed and CAN print. The print goes through `_printLiveness` → `io.writeln` → stderr in headless (per the CliIO contract "route [CliIO.writeln] diagnostics to stderr"). So stdout stays clean IF the host io is wired to stderr. Is that guaranteed for stream-json mode? The doc comment says "should be non-interactive and route CliIO.writeln diagnostics to stderr" — it's a contract on the host wiring, not enforced. The pre-existing tier-2 line has the same exposure, and the HEP/stream-json tests pass today (gh-1198 shipped with the same channel). So E5 risk is inherited, not new. The missing E5 IT is a test-coverage gap vs the ticket's stated test plan (IT-H1..H3 "header race pin"). Since behavior is safe by the same channel as tier-2, I'd rate the missing E5 test as a SUGGESTION/IMPORTANT-borderline. Given the ticket explicitly promised "IT-H1..H3: abort-mid-heartbeat cleanliness (heartbeat line never interleaves into a JSON/HEP first line — header race pin)" and no such test exists, that's a legitimate coverage gap worth flagging — IMPORTANT? Hmm. The PR description's test list doesn't claim an E5 test: "headless ITs — stdout growth under a thinking-only stream (AC3), event-silent silence, tier-2-only dead window, non-reasoning byte-identity (AC5), `--stream-thinking` unchanged, tool-row disarm/re-arm (E2), line-mode parity, compaction window (E3)". I don't see an explicit E4 abort test in the new tests either. The lifecycle `stop()` UT covers disarm-on-stop; the `_printLiveness` `_cli._exited` guard covers the print-after-exit. But "abort mid-heartbeat → no line after the abort banner" is not directly tested. Again a promised-in-ticket test that's missing.

Now, AC1 in the ticket: "the moment a renderable byte prints (text delta / tool line / streamed thinking), the heartbeat disarms. UT with fake clock + fake event sink." ✓ covered by UTs.

AC3: "headless E2E: a fake provider streaming thinking-only deltas for 6 minutes leaves the captured stdout byte-count monotonically growing (heartbeat cadence visible); no provider error; run completes." The IT test uses `streamLivenessTickForTest()` manual ticks rather than real timer-driven 6-minute flow — acceptable harness-level equivalent (fake clock + manual tick seam). The ticket says "fake clock + fake event sink" for AC1 UT; AC3 E2E with real timers would need 6 minutes — the IT uses the tick seam. Reasonable adaptation.

def audit_dict(
    knobs: TimeoutKnobs,
    ladder: ProgressLadder,
    outcome: str | None,
    progress_bytes: int | None = None,
    liveness_bytes: int | None = None,
):
    """Trial-artifact audit record (what extended, when, why).

    Issue #1185 AC6: when the caller can read the progress stream, it also
    passes the final sample size (`progress_bytes`) and the bytes inside it
    that are fa's OWN `⏳` liveness lines (`liveness_bytes`,
    [liveness_bytes_of]) — harness-originated prints the pane counter
    counts as progress. Documented, not subtracted: the model legitimately
    reads its own logs, so separating the two streams perfectly is not
    attempted; the audit makes the inflation visible per trial.
    """
    record = {
        "issue": 1122,
        "policy": (
            "progress-watch"
            if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
            else ("progress-aware" if knobs.progress_extension else "flat-cap")
        ),
        "outcome": outcome or "completed",
        "knobs": {
            "base_sec": knobs.base_sec,
            "progress_extension": knobs.progress_extension,
            "idle_window_sec": knobs.idle_window_sec,
            "ceiling_multiplier": knobs.ceiling_multiplier,
            "ceiling_sec": knobs.ceiling_sec,
            # Round-3 (issue #1392): effective watch knobs render in the
            # audit only when the gap-aware decision is active.
            **(
                {
                    "stall_gap_sec": knobs.watch_stall_gap_sec,
                    "abs_ceiling_sec": knobs.watch_abs_ceiling_sec,
                }
                if getattr(knobs, "progress_watch", False)
                else {}
            ),
        },
        "last_progress_sec": round(ladder.last_progress_at, 3),
        "last_output_bytes": ladder.last_bytes,
        "deadline_sec": round(ladder.kill_at, 3),
        "extensions": ladder.events,
    }
    if progress_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_sample_bytes"] = progress_bytes
    if liveness_bytes is not None:
        record["progress_liveness_bytes"] = liveness_bytes
        record["progress_note"] = (
            "progress_liveness_bytes = the agent's own liveness status "
            "lines inside the progress sample (issue #1185 AC6): "
            "harness-originated bytes the pane counter counts as progress"
        )
    return record


# The liveness status line's grep anchor (gh-1055): every harness-originated
# reminder/escalation line carries it; nothing else the agent emits does.
_LIVENESS_ANCHOR = "⏳"


def liveness_bytes_of(stream: str | bytes | None) -> int | None:
    """Bytes of `⏳` liveness lines inside a progress stream (AC6 helper).

    None propagates: an unreadable stream must not fabricate a zero (the
    audit then just omits the field).

    Byte accounting splits on `'\\n'` only (reproducible against `wc -c`):
    a matched line counts its full bytes — a `\\r` stays in the line — plus
    exactly the one newline it ends with, and a final unterminated line
    counts without the newline. `str.splitlines()` would also split on
    `\\r`, `\\v`, `\\x85`, … and silently miscount against the byte total.
    """
    if stream is None:
        return None
    if isinstance(stream, bytes):
        stream = stream.decode("utf-8", errors="replace")
    total = 0
    lines = stream.split("\n")
    for index, line in enumerate(lines):
        if _LIVENESS_ANCHOR in line:
            total += len(line.encode("utf-8"))
            if index < len(lines) - 1:
                total += 1  # the newline this line ends with
    return total

# Runs the fa coding agent against the Terminal-Bench dataset family on
# the Harbor framework: 2.0 / 2.1 / 3.0 / 4.0 from ONE dispatch surface
# (issue #1124; the 4.0 path is issue #147). The `dataset` input takes a
# family label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or a full Harbor dataset id — resolved
# and validated by bench/harbor_fa/families.py (unknown or version-less
# specs fail fast; never a silent fallback). The default dispatch is the
# 2.1 family (issue #1316: the bench migrates to Terminal-Bench 2.x /
# Harbor — supersedes #1124 AC4's 4.0 default; 4.0/3.0/2.0 stay one input
# away). CPU shards run the default Harbor `docker` sandbox on
# ubuntu-latest (GH runners ship docker — no Modal/cloud dependency for
# the default dispatch, #1316); GPU tasks always route to a modal shard
# and cpu-runner/cpu-env keep the self-hosted + modal dispatch reachable.
# Results upload
# to Harbor Hub — the current leaderboard source (tbench.ai; 4.0 is the
# leaderboard dataset). The legacy terminal-bench-core 0.1.1 path lives
# in bench.yml.
#
# Same bundle/env contract as the legacy bench: `dart build cli` Linux
# bundle + FA_PROVIDER_TYPE=zai env-provider-preconfig (glm-5.3-flash),
# secrets env-only and never echoed (keys pass base64-encoded into the
# task container; CI masks both raw and base64 forms).
#
# Smoke first: dispatch with tasks=<family smoke>, attempts=1 (smoke task
# per family in docs/bench.md). Full (tasks-less) runs of the
# intermediate families (2.0/2.1/3.0) additionally require
# confirm-full-run: true — a full family sweep is hours of GPU + LLM
# spend. Full 4.0 dispatches keep their historical no-confirmation
# behaviour (issue #1124 AC4).
#
# Secrets (owner-provisioned; the workflow never hardcodes them):
#   FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY       — z.ai key for glm-5.3-flash (shared with bench.yml)
#   MODAL_TOKEN_ID/SECRET  — Modal token for the GPU shard (verified live)
#   HARBOR_API_KEY         — Harbor Hub upload key; upload step skips (with a
#                            warning) when absent, run artifacts keep results.

on:
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Comma fnmatch globs narrowing the dataset (empty = full dataset; use the family smoke task first — docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Terminal-Bench family: label (2.0/2.1/3.0/4.0) or full Harbor id (see bench/harbor_fa/families.py); default 2.1 (issue #1316)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench/terminal-bench-2-1@latest'
      confirm-full-run:
        description: 'Required true for full (tasks-less) runs of 2.0/2.1/3.0 — smoke first (docs/bench.md)'
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false
      model:
        description: 'Model id recorded with the run (provider preconfig is authoritative for fa)'
        required: false
        default: 'glm-5.3-flash'
      attempts:
        description: 'harbor --n-attempts per trial (-k)'
        required: false
        default: '5'
      n-concurrent:
        description: 'harbor --n-concurrent trials (1 = z.ai rate-limit safe)'
        required: false
        default: '1'
      shards:
        description: 'Shard count for CPU tasks (~4 tasks/shard keeps each job under the 6h window)'
        required: false
        default: '16'
      cpu-env:
        description: 'Harbor env for CPU shards (docker default — issue #1316; modal for the self-hosted path)'
        required: false
        default: 'docker'
      cpu-runner:
        description: 'Runner label hosting the harbor CLI (ubuntu-latest default — GH runners ship docker; self-hosted for the modal path)'
        required: false
        default: 'ubuntu-latest'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared task caps)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds the runner for hours; queue a second dispatch
# instead of stacking them. One group across the whole family: harbor
# runs serialize even when different dataset versions are dispatched
# back-to-back.
concurrency:
  group: bench-harbor
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & shard dataset
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      cpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.cpu_count }}
      gpu_count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.gpu_count }}
      family: ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }}
      dataset: ${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).
      - uses: dart-lang/setup-dart@6afc89df92d6eb3834022f73cd65adc8cdfcb92d # v1
        with:
          sdk: stable

      - run: dart pub get

      # Resolve the dispatch input (family label, bare version, or full
      # Harbor id) to the canonical dataset id; unknown or version-less
      # specs fail fast here, before any download.
      - name: Resolve Terminal-Bench family
        id: family
        env:
          DATASET: ${{ inputs.dataset }}
        run: python bench/harbor_fa/families.py resolve "$DATASET"

      # Cost guard (issue #1124 E3): full runs of the intermediate
      # families are hours of GPU + LLM spend — require explicit
      # confirmation. Smoke runs (non-empty tasks) and 4.0 (the
      # historical default, AC4) are unaffected.
      - name: Confirm full intermediate-family run
        if: steps.family.outputs.family != '4.0' && inputs.confirm-full-run != true
        env:
          TASKS: ${{ inputs.tasks }}
          ATTEMPTS: ${{ inputs.attempts }}
        run: |
          # split_tasks.py strips each comma-glob before use, so " ", ",",
          # " , " all normalize to zero globs = a FULL dataset run. Judge
          # emptiness on that same normalization, not the raw input.
          if [ -z "$(printf %s "$TASKS" | tr -d '[:space:],')" ]; then
            echo "::error::Full run of Terminal-Bench ${{ steps.family.outputs.family }} (${{ steps.family.outputs.dataset }}, ~${{ steps.family.outputs.tasks }} tasks x $ATTEMPTS attempts) requires confirm-full-run: true. Smoke first: tasks=${{ steps.family.outputs.smoke }}, attempts=1 (docs/bench.md)."
            exit 1
          fi

      # Same bundle as bench/terminal_bench/run.sh: tar the bundle/ dir so
      # the adapter extracts bin/fah at the top level of /opt/fa.
      - name: Build fa CLI bundle (Linux)
        run: |
          bundle_dir="$(mktemp -d)/fa-bundle"
          dart build cli --target=bin/fah.dart --output="$bundle_dir"
          tar -czf fa-bundle.tar.gz -C "$bundle_dir/bundle" .

      - name: Upload fa bundle
        uses: actions/upload-artifact@043fb46d1a93c77aae656e7c1c64a875d1fc6a0a # v7.0.1
        with:
          name: fa-bundle
          path: fa-bundle.tar.gz

      # terminal-bench-era note: harbor is fine on 3.13; typer-based CLIs
      # break on 3.14.
      - uses: actions/setup-python@5fda3b95a4ea91299a34e894583c3862153e4b97 # v7.0.0
        with:
          python-version: '3.13'

      # Pinned: the adapter targets the 0.23.0 BaseInstalledAgent contract.
      - run: pip install 'harbor[modal]==0.23.0'

      # Same gate as bench.yml: stdlib-only bench script tests. Two
      # discovery roots: bench/terminal_bench (legacy scripts + the
      # harbor parity suite from #1122 — terminal-bench is installed
      # just for the legacy-adapter import surface) …
